name: DS18B20+
title: DS18B20: 1-Wire digital thermometer, 9- to 12-bit resolution, -55 °C to +125 °C
summary: A temperature sensor that reports degrees Celsius as a 9- to 12-bit two's-complement reading over a single-wire 1-Wire bus. Each part carries a laser-programmed 64-bit ROM code, so many sensors can share one data line and one ground, and it can take its power from the data line itself (parasite power) or from a 3.0 V to 5.5 V supply on VDD. Error is ±0.5 °C max from -10 °C to +85 °C; a 12-bit conversion takes up to 750 ms. Upper and lower alarm thresholds and the resolution setting are held in on-chip EEPROM. Packages are 3-pin TO-92 (DS18B20), 8-pin µSOP (DS18B20U) and 8-pin 150 mil SO (DS18B20Z).
key_figures: 93.75 ms max at 9 bits to 750 ms max at 12 bits

circuits.title: Supplying the parasite-powered DS18B20 during temperature conversions
circuits.description: The sensor runs with no supply of its own: VDD and GND both go to ground and DQ sits on the 1-Wire bus, held high by a 4.7 kΩ resistor to VPU. A P-channel MOSFET from VPU to the bus, switched by the microcontroller, shorts out the resistor while a conversion or an EEPROM copy runs, so the part gets the current it then needs. The bus continues to further 1-Wire devices.

parts.value: strong pullup gate drive from µP

circuits.title: Powering the DS18B20 with an external supply
circuits.description: The sensor takes its power from a separate VDD supply and uses the bus for data only. DQ is on the 1-Wire bus with a 4.7 kΩ pullup to VPU, GND goes to ground, and no strong pullup is needed, so the bus can carry other traffic during a conversion.

operation.text: A 64-bit ROM holds the part's own code. The scratchpad holds the 2-byte temperature result, the 1-byte TH and TL alarm thresholds and the 1-byte configuration register; TH, TL and configuration have EEPROM copies that keep their values with power off. Internal blocks are the temperature sensor, the parasite power circuit with its capacitor CPP, a supply sense, memory control logic and an 8-bit CRC generator.

Resolution is set to 9, 10, 11 or 12 bits, and is 12 bits by default at power-up. The part starts up idle at low power. A Convert T (44h) command starts one conversion; the result goes to the temperature register and the part returns to idle. With an external supply, read slots sent after Convert T return 0 while the conversion runs and 1 once it is complete. On parasite power this status cannot be read, since the strong pullup holds the bus high throughout. The output is in Celsius only.

After each conversion, register bits 11 to 4 are compared with TH and TL (8-bit two's complement). A reading at or below TL, or at or above TH, sets the alarm flag; the next conversion clears it if the condition is gone. An Alarm Search (ECh) is answered only by parts with the flag set. After a change to TH or TL, a new conversion confirms the alarm. Without the alarm in use, TH and TL serve as two bytes of general-purpose memory.

The part runs from a supply on VDD, or on parasite power with VDD grounded: it draws charge from DQ while the bus is high and stores some on CPP to run while the bus is low. That is enough for most operations within the timing and voltage limits. During a conversion or a scratchpad-to-EEPROM copy the current rises up to 1.5 mA, more than the weak pullup can give, so the bus is then pulled straight to the rail, as by a MOSFET. The strong pullup must be on within 10 µs max of a Convert T (44h) or Copy Scratchpad (48h) and stay on for tCONV or tWR (10 ms); nothing else may use the bus meanwhile. With an external supply no MOSFET pullup is needed and the bus stays free during conversions.
Above +100 °C parasite power is not recommended: leakage grows and communication may fail. An external supply is the recommended choice where such temperatures are likely.

Skip ROM (CCh), then Read Power Supply (B4h), then a read slot: a parasite-powered part pulls the bus low during the slot and an externally powered part leaves it high. A low tells the master to apply the strong pullup during conversions.
The least significant byte of the 64-bit ROM code is the family code, 28h; the next 48 bits are a unique serial number and the top byte is a CRC of the first 56 bits.

Write Scratchpad (4Eh) loads bytes 2, 3 and 4, least significant bit of byte 2 first; all three bytes must go before a reset or they may be corrupted. Read Scratchpad (BEh) returns from bit 0 of byte 0 through byte 8 (the CRC) and can be cut short by a reset. Copy Scratchpad (48h) stores bytes 2 to 4 in EEPROM; on parasite power it needs the strong pullup within 10 µs and for at least 10 ms. EEPROM contents are loaded into the scratchpad at power-up and on Recall E2 (B8h); read slots after Recall E2 return 0 while it runs and 1 when done.

The ROM code's top byte and scratchpad byte 8 are CRCs (ROM: of its first 56 bits; scratchpad: of bytes 0 to 7, so it changes with the data). The master checks them itself; the part never blocks a command on a mismatch. The generator is a shift register with XOR taps, started at 0; data goes in least significant bit first, then the received CRC byte, after which all stages read 0 if the data are good.

One master and one or more slaves share a single data line; the DS18B20 is always a slave. Each device drives the line through an open-drain or three-state port. DQ is open drain: its equivalent is a 5 µA typ current sink from DQ to ground, a 100 Ω MOSFET pull-down for transmit, and a receive buffer. The bus needs an external pullup of about 5 kΩ, so it idles high. A transaction can pause indefinitely between bits as long as the bus rests high; holding it low longer than 480 µs resets every device on it. Data and commands go least significant bit first.

Every access is initialization (reset, then presence), a ROM command with its data, then a function command with its data; the part does not respond if a step is missing or out of order. After Search ROM or Alarm Search the master starts again with initialization. Read ROM collides if more than one slave is present, as does Skip ROM followed by Read Scratchpad. Skip ROM followed by Convert T starts every sensor converting at once.

The master pulls the bus low for at least 480 µs, then releases it and listens for at least 480 µs. The pullup brings the bus high; the DS18B20 waits 15 µs to 60 µs after that edge and pulls the bus low for 60 µs to 240 µs as its presence pulse.

Each slot lasts at least 60 µs, with at least 1 µs of recovery between slots, and starts with the master pulling the bus low. For a 1 the master lets go within 15 µs; for a 0 it holds the bus low to the end of the slot (60 µs to 120 µs). The DS18B20 samples between 15 µs and 60 µs after the slot starts: high is a 1, low a 0.

The part sends data only in read slots, which the master generates right after Read Scratchpad or Read Power Supply, and may generate after Convert T or Recall E2 for status. A slot lasts at least 60 µs with at least 1 µs recovery; the master pulls the bus low for at least 1 µs and releases it. The part sends a 1 by leaving the bus high and a 0 by holding it low, releasing it by the slot's end. Its data are valid for 15 µs from the falling edge, so the master's own low time, the rise time and its sample point together must come within 15 µs; margin is best with a short low time, a fast rise and the sample late in the 15 µs.

Several parasite-powered sensors, one read: reset and presence, Match ROM (55h) with the 64-bit code, Convert T (44h) with the strong pullup held for tCONV, then reset and presence, Match ROM with the code, Read Scratchpad (BEh), nine bytes read and the CRC of the first eight checked against byte 9, the read repeated on a mismatch. One parasite-powered sensor, set-up: reset, Skip ROM (CCh), Write Scratchpad (4Eh) with TH, TL and configuration; reset, Skip ROM, Read Scratchpad and CRC check; reset, Skip ROM, Copy Scratchpad (48h) with the strong pullup held at least 10 ms.
